predecessors.note: "Founded in 1647 when the Harari refused to accept Imām ʿUmardīn Ādam and broke from the Imamate of Aussa under ʿAli ibn Daʿud." The Adal Sultanate (to 1577) and the Harar sultanate of Cliopatria (1547-1578) came earlier.

land.text: Harar and its plateau under Emir Abdullah II

successors.note: "Negus Menelik afterwards occupied and annexed the city of Harar" after the Battle of Chelenqo; Makonnen governed "Hararge and the adjacent Harar region".

capitals.name: Harar (Gey)
capitals.note: "The city of Harar Gey served as its sole capital."

rulers.name: ʿAli ibn Daʿud
rulers.note: Rulers table of the Emirate of Harar page.

rulers.name: Muhammad ibn ʿAli ʿAbd al-Shakur
rulers.note: Followed by the Egyptian Khedivate 1875-1882 and the British occupation 1882-1884 (Egyptian governors Rauf Pasha 1875-1878, Ridhwan Pasha 1878-1880, Nadi Pasha 1880-1883, Ridha Pasha 1883-1884).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria lacks the Emirate). The page: "the Harar Emirate made up the area between the rivers Awash and Shebelle" (League of Nations, 1935), the Ogaden a tributary, and "Originally it included present-day Somalia and the south of eastern Ethiopia, including Arsi Province"; Garads and Malaks were recorded as far west as Dawaro in the 19th century. I draw the plateau with a 150 km radius, far less than the page's widest claims, because Oromo and Somali clans "gradually annexed Harari land" from the 17th century. No area figure on the page.

correction.text: Harar and its plateau under Emir Abdullah II

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. After the Egyptian (1875-1884) and British (1882-1884) occupations, Emir ʿAbdullah II ruled 1884-1887. The page gives no territory for this reign; the city and its plateau are drawn. Egyptian-held Harar 1875-1883 has no keyframe: the ledger removes and returns the land.

ledger.note: 1647: Harar breaks from the Imamate of Aussa under Emir ʿAli ibn Daʿud. "The Emirate of Harar was a Muslim kingdom founded in 1647"; "the Harari refused to accept Imām ʿUmardīn Ādam". The page names Harar, not a boundary.

18th century: Oromo and Somali clans erode the outer lands. "Oromo and Somali clans paid tax to the Emirate into the 18th century, even as they gradually annexed Harari land"; Oromo raids reached the Asmadin Gate in 1662. A process with no dated step: 1700 is a bridge. Revised by fx-41 (window request R096): the region was the whole keyframe (Harar region plus the 150 km disk), so the Emirate held 0 of its 316 cells from 1700 to 1875 although the infobox gives 'Sovereign kingdom (1647-1875)' and the same page has the clans only 'gradually' annexing land, penetrating 'even the lands held by the Harari, a short distance from the town' (late 18th century). Now only the 174-cell outer ring is lost; the 142-cell core is kept to the 1875 loss (ledger/2).

region.text: the outer lands of the Emirate: the 150 km disk round Harar without the 100 km Harar region (the plateau round the city, 142 of the 316 cells), which stays Harari

ledger.note: 11 October 1875: Egypt seizes Harar. The page: Egypt "seized Harar on 11 October 1875" under Muhammad Rauf Pasha; the infobox gives Egyptian rule 1875-1884, the rulers table 1875-1882.

1884: the British withdraw and ʿAbdullah II rules. "The British Empire defeated the Khedivate and occupied its territories in 1882 including Harar"; "the British withdrew from Harar in 1884" (Hewett Treaty). Emir ʿAbdullah ibn Muhammad reigned 1884-1887.

9 January 1887: Menelik annexes Harar. "an engagement fought on 9 January 1887 between the Abyssinian army of Shewa" and the Emir; "Negus Menelik afterwards occupied and annexed the city of Harar"; "With the occupation, the independence of Harar came to an end." The Ethiopian Empire dossier dates the annexation 6 January 1887.
January 1887: the Emirate of Harar ends; the infobox result is "Collapse of the Emirate of Harar and absorption into the Ethiopian Empire".

wars.name: Egyptian conquest of Harar
wars.outcome: Egypt seized Harar on 11 October 1875; the British occupied it after defeating the Khedivate in 1882 and withdrew in 1884 under the Hewett Treaty.
wars.note: Infobox Egyptian subjection 1875-1884, rulers table 1875-1882 and British occupation 1882-1884.

wars.name: Battle of Chelenqo
wars.outcome: Menelik's Shewan army defeated Emir ʿAbdullah II on 9 January 1887 and annexed Harar; Makonnen was made governor of Hararge. The page notes an earlier Shewan defeat at Hirna in late 1886.
wars.note: The Ethiopian Empire dossier (af-01-b) has 6 January 1887.

wars.name: Oromo raids on Harar
wars.outcome: Raids reached the Asmadin Gate in 1662 and killed Emir ʿAli's son; Oromo and Somali clans gradually annexed Harari land while paying tax.

certainty.note: Only the city is a fixed point; the page gives frontier descriptions by rivers (Awash, Shebelle) from a 1935 report.

sources.title: Emirate of Harar
sources.note: Identity, founding 1647 from the Imamate of Aussa, extent between the Awash and the Shebelle, Oromo raids 1662, Egyptian occupation from 11 October 1875, British 1882-1884, rulers 1647-1887, annexation 1887. No area.

sources.title: Battle of Chelenqo
sources.note: 9 January 1887, Menelik of Shewa defeats Emir Abdullah II and annexes Harar; Makonnen governs Hararge.

notes:
New dossier: Cliopatria's Adal Sultanate (to 1546) and Sultanate of Harar (1547-1578) precede it, the Imamate of Aussa (1577-1647) intervenes; the Emirate of Harar (1647-1887) has no Cliopatria row. Pages opened: Emirate of Harar, Battle of Chelenqo (2). Disagreements: Egyptian rule 1875-1884 (infobox) or 1875-1882 (rulers table); annexation 9 January 1887 (Chelenqo page) or 6 January (Ethiopian Empire dossier); the page says the Emirate 'originally included present-day Somalia and the south of eastern Ethiopia, including Arsi Province', which is wider than any later extent and is not drawn. Not on the pages: vassals (the Ogaden as tributary in a 1935 League of Nations passage), the Hewett treaty's terms, coastal Zeila/Berbera (trade partners only). Counterparts needing dossiers: imamate-of-aussa (1577-1647; Wikipedia 'Aussa Sultanate' history), 'Oromo' (peoples). The Egyptian side (Harar 1875-1884) is also in me-10's Khedivate dossier.
Gazetteer: all names resolved (Harar (region), Harar place).
